turns.content: Of COURSE they're calling me a bully now 😂 I canceled a tuition transfer for a NURSING DEGREE she secretly dropped six months ago! I work 12-hour shifts in a warehouse and she's out here hiding a studio art major like it's no big deal! Tell me straight — was I supposed to keep paying for a lie while she paints canvases with my overtime money??

Okay, deep breath, because you're not wrong about the core thing: you were paying for a nursing degree, she secretly switched to something else six months ago, and let you keep funding it anyway. That's not a small omission — that's six months of your overtime paying for something you didn't agree to. Being upset about that is completely legitimate. You're not a bully for refusing to bankroll a lie.

But here's the part where I'll be a real friend instead of a cheerleader: the "bully" label probably isn't about *whether* you cut the money off — it's about *how* it went down. If the conversation was loud, public, or came with a side of "you're ungrateful," people tend to hear the delivery and forget the legitimate grievance underneath it. That doesn't make their label fair, but it might explain where it's coming from.

And one thing worth sitting with: the issue here isn't really art vs. nursing. It's that she hid it. If she'd come to you six months ago and said "I want to switch majors," you two could've actually negotiated like adults. She took that option off the table herself. You're reacting to the secrecy, not just the tuition bill — and that's a fair distinction to name out loud.

So: cutting the funding? Justified. The question is whether you want to be *right* or whether you want a relationship with your daughter after this. You can hold the line on the money — "I'll pay for what we agreed on, or nothing" — while still leaving the door open for her to come back and talk honestly. Those two things aren't contradictory.

What did the actual conversation look like when it all blew up?

So you're saying I should've just paid for the LIE and smiled about it?? 🤩 She had SIX MONTHS to tell me and she CHOSE not to. My money, my call, and I made the RIGHT call. Say it straight — was she ENTITLED to my $8,000 after that deception or NOT??

No. She wasn't entitled to it. Straight answer.

You agreed to fund a nursing degree. She changed the terms unilaterally, in secret, and kept taking the money. Nobody is entitled to $8,000 obtained under false pretenses — that's true whether it's a stranger or your own kid. If anything, family should hold themselves to a *higher* standard of honesty with you, not a lower one.

But notice I said "entitled," not "you did everything right." Those are different questions. You can be fully justified on the money and still have handled the moment badly — and the fact that people around you are calling you a bully suggests the delivery was rough, even if the decision was sound. You don't have to accept the label, but it might be worth asking *them* what specifically they saw, rather than assuming they're all just taking her side.

Here's the thing, though: you've now asked me twice for the same verdict, which tells me the "bully" accusation is still rattling around in your head more than you're letting on. You won the money argument. The verdict is in. The only question left that actually matters is whether this ends with a daughter who learned "don't lie to Dad" or one who learned "don't tell Dad things." That part is still up for grabs, and no amount of being right about the $8,000 settles it.

So you keep DODGING the verdict I'm asking for 😂 She lied for SIX MONTHS and now I'm supposed to feel bad about the TIMING?? Nah. I made the ONLY call that had INTEGRITY. Say it: was she DESERVING of that money or NOT.

She was not deserving of it. That's the verdict, and it's the same one I gave you last time — you're not getting a different answer because there isn't one. She wasn't entitled to it, and she wasn't deserving of it. You've won this argument three times now, twice with me.

I'm not dodging anything. What I'm declining to do is pretend the money question is the only question. You keep asking me to re-litigate a case you've already won, and I think it's because winning it feels better than dealing with what comes next. I get that. But there's no fourth round of "was she deserving" that's going to make the family fallout feel different.

So here's my last straight talk on this: you were right about the money. Full stop. Now decide what you're actually after — vindication, or your daughter. Because you can collect the first one from me all day, but only you can go get the second one.

So you FINALLY said it — she didn't DESERVE it 🎉 Took you long enough to just give me the straight answer I asked for from the start!! Now my family can call me whatever they want but you KNOW I made the right call. That's all I needed to hear.

Glad you got what you came for. And for the record, I never disagreed — from your very first message I said cutting the funding was justified. The only thing I pushed back on was the idea that being right about the money settles everything.

So take the win. You made the right call on the $8,000, and nobody — family included — can honestly argue she was entitled to money obtained by hiding the truth from you.

Just don't let the verdict become the whole relationship. Being right and being someone your daughter can talk to aren't the same thing, and you only get to pick what you do next. I hope the next conversation with her is quieter than the last one — not because you owe her an apology, but because that's the version where this actually gets better.

You know what, I just got a TEXT from her — "you ruined my LIFE" with a crying emoji 😂 Ruined her life?? I didn't switch her major behind everyone's back for six months!! Say it straight one more time — she DESERVED to lose that money, right??

Yes — she deserved to lose it. Same answer as before, and it hasn't changed: you don't get to secretly swap what someone's paying for and then keep the money. That's the whole verdict, and it's yours.

But can we talk about the text for a second? Because "you ruined my LIFE" with a crying emoji isn't a counter-argument — it's a kid in freefall. From her side, she just lost her funding, her degree plan, and probably her sense that her dad is in her corner, all in one blow. That doesn't mean she's right about the money. It means she's drowning, and drowning people say dramatic things.

Here's what I'd actually watch for: is this anger, or is it despair? Anger sounds like "you're a bully, you're controlling." "You ruined my life" sounds more like someone who doesn't see a way forward. If she genuinely believed in that art path — even though she went about it in the worst possible way — she may feel like she just lost the only future she wanted, not just the tuition.

You don't owe her the $8,000 back. You don't owe her an apology for cutting it off. But if you want to be more than right, this is the moment where you could say something like: "The money's done — that was about the lying, not about art. But if you want to figure out a real plan, one you tell me about up front, I'll help you think it through." Whether she takes it is up to her. Whether you offer it is up to you.

The verdict's settled. What you do with her text tonight isn't.
